Visual predictive checks

Source: vignettes/articles/plot-vpc.Rmd
plot-vpc.Rmd
library(erplots)
library(emaxnls)
library(erglm)

The mini-grammar for VPC plots is considerably simpler than the one for exposure-response plots.

Binary response

By exposure 

mod <- erglm_model(ae1 ~ aucss, erglm_data, family = binomial())

The default approach for binary outcomes is to bin the exposure variable by quartiles, and then show the confidence interval for the response rate for both observed and simulated:

erglm_data |> 
  er_vpc(exposure = aucss, response = ae1) |>
  er_vpc_add_observed() |>
  er_vpc_add_simulated(model = mod, seed = 1234) |>
  plot()

By continuous covariate

Continuous plot_by does not have to be the same as the exposure variable:

erglm_data |> 
  er_vpc(exposure = aucss, response = ae1, plot_by = weight) |>
  er_vpc_add_observed() |>
  er_vpc_add_simulated(model = mod, seed = 1234) |>
  plot()

By discrete covariate 

mod <- erglm_model(ae1 ~ aucss + sex, erglm_data, family = binomial())

erglm_data |> 
  er_vpc(exposure = aucss, response = ae1, plot_by = sex) |>
  er_vpc_add_observed() |>
  er_vpc_add_simulated(model = mod, seed = 1234) |>
  plot()

Continuous response

By exposure 

mod <- emax_nls(
  structural_model = rsp_1 ~ exp_1,
  covariate_model = list(E0 ~ 1, Emax ~ 1, logEC50 ~ 1),
  data = emax_df
)

For continuous outcomes, more options are available. It is possible to adopt the same approach as we did for binary outcomes, and it does work:

emax_df |> 
  er_vpc(exposure = exp_1, response = rsp_1) |> 
  er_vpc_add_observed() |> 
  er_vpc_add_simulated(model = mod, seed = 1234) |>
  plot()

However, this approach only considers whether the model is correctly predicting the mean response within each bin.

As an alternative, we can switch to a distributional approach:

emax_df |> 
  er_vpc(
    exposure = exp_1, 
    response = rsp_1, 
    response_type = "continuous"
  ) |> 
  er_vpc_add_observed(style = er_style_vpc_observed_quantile_line) |> 
  er_vpc_add_simulated(
    model = mod, 
    seed = 1234, 
    style = er_style_vpc_simulated_quantile_ribbon
  ) |>
  plot()

For more detailed examination, it is also possible to display nonparametric confidence intervals for the observed data quantiles, plotted (like the default mean/errorbar pair) at each bin’s numeric median on the exposure scale.

emax_df |> 
  er_vpc(
    exposure = exp_1, 
    response = rsp_1, 
    response_type = "continuous"
  ) |> 
  er_vpc_add_observed(style = er_style_vpc_observed_quantile_errorbar) |> 
  er_vpc_add_simulated(
    model = mod, 
    seed = 1234, 
    style = er_style_vpc_simulated_quantile_errorbar
  ) |>
  plot()

By continuous covariate

Continuous plot_by variables can be something other than the exposure:

mod <- emax_nls(
  structural_model = rsp_1 ~ exp_1,
  covariate_model = list(E0 ~ cnt_a, Emax ~ 1, logEC50 ~ 1),
  data = emax_df
)

emax_df |> 
  er_vpc(
    exposure = exp_1, 
    response = rsp_1, 
    response_type = "continuous",
    plot_by = cnt_a
  ) |> 
  er_vpc_add_observed(style = er_style_vpc_observed_quantile_errorbar) |> 
  er_vpc_add_simulated(
    model = mod, 
    seed = 1234, 
    style = er_style_vpc_simulated_quantile_errorbar
  ) |>
  plot()



emax_df |> 
  er_vpc(
    exposure = exp_1, 
    response = rsp_1, 
    response_type = "continuous",
    plot_by = cnt_a
  ) |> 
  er_vpc_add_observed(style = er_style_vpc_observed_quantile_errorbar) |> 
  er_vpc_add_simulated(
    model = mod, 
    seed = 1234, 
    style = er_style_vpc_simulated_quantile_ribbon
  ) |>
  plot()

By discrete covariate 

mod <- erglm_model(
  biomarker_change ~ aucss + sex, erglm_data, family = gaussian()
)

erglm_data |> 
  er_vpc(exposure = aucss, response = biomarker_change, plot_by = sex) |>
  er_vpc_add_observed() |>
  er_vpc_add_simulated(model = mod, seed = 1234) |>
  plot()
